method: microspectrophotometry of visual pigments in single photoreceptors (MSP)

source.authors: Loew ER, Fleishman LJ, Foster RG, Provencio I
source.title: Visual pigments and oil droplets in diurnal lizards: a comparative study of Caribbean anoles

quote: all anoline species examined possessed at least four vitamin-A1-based visual pigments
note: Four classes: LWS, MWS, SWS, UVS; A. carolinensis uses vitamin A2 for LWS. UVS spectra were not recorded in five species and are inferred from C2 oil droplets. The quote is as reported by the fetch of the PDF.

taxon: Anolis carolinensis, A. cristatellus, A. sagrei
value: four cone pigment classes (UVS, SWS, MWS, LWS)
method: oil droplet colour as a marker of cone class, with microspectrophotometry cited from earlier work

source.title: Variability in oil droplet numbers and proportions in the retinas of anole lizards
source.journal: Frontiers in Amphibian and Reptile Science

quote: The two remaining classes of large single cone contain the green droplet and either the LWS or MWS visual pigment.
note: Colourless droplets go with UVS and SWS single cones; double cones and one single-cone class carry LWS. Earlier MSP values near 565, 495, 465 and 365 nm are cited in the introduction.
